## 1 · Resolve the Scene and the Available Tools

Continue the same MOVIOLA directing task through 3D preparation.

- Keep the resolved Project, Draft, Scene and intended Cut IDs together. The Scene owns its own source: a glTF package the server builds (step 4), or an older .blend revision, which stays readable but can no longer be published or selected. Each Cut owns its setup and chosen Sketch. Reuse asset revisions across Scenes, and start a recurring location in an independent working copy.
- Inspect the tools actually advertised by this MOVIOLA connection and the local Blender connection. Remote tools own server state, selection and Scene assembly; the local connection owns camera application and rendering. Assembling, reviewing and publishing the Scene (step 4) needs only MOVIOLA tools: build_scene_source, get_scene_source_build and publish_scene_source_build. render_cut_setup draws a Cut setup of a server-built source without Blender, but no Cut setup can be made on such a source yet (step 5). A loaded skill does not install Blender or add MCP tools.
- Use get_scene_3d_state with the explicit draft_id and sceneId to read the saved mode, currentRevisionId and references checked against current inputs. A saved get_scene projection alone does not prove freshness. set_scene_3d_mode selects 2d or 3d without starting generation; do not mutate scene3d through update_scene. Both recommend and advanced profiles expose these operations. Source connection issuance, revision listing/selection and upload receipts are available in both profiles. Cut setup listing/selection, render connection issuance, candidate image reads and explicit Sketch adoption are also available in both profiles.
- When a local Blender connection is available, use its installed Scene 3D workflow and supported moviola_vcam modules: scene_commands, scene_cloud, cut_setup, sketch_capture and sketch_cloud. Resolve their installed inputs rather than copying test fixture destinations or writing substitute transfer logic. If an execution capability is missing, finish the analysis possible with available references and report that step as pending.
- **Choose one execution route per 3D Sketch request before any paid call; the saved 3D mode does not choose it.** Ordinary generate_storyboard here means a call without prepareReferences=true; on a 3D Scene whose current source is a .blend revision it queues a Mac worker Job, a v2 Scene whose requested Cuts all have a Still framing is drawn on the server with no worker or Blender, and any other 3D Scene is refused as the last paragraph of this step says. Reference preparation (step 2) is allowed on every route. A session the Mac worker launched — its prompt hands over that queued Generate request and forbids ordinary generate_storyboard — is the worker: it runs the interactive route for its own Scenes and never queues the workflow again. Anywhere else, the interactive Blender route, which serves only a Scene whose current source is still a .blend revision, needs all three here: a Blender MCP Python executor in this session, exactly one enabled moviola_vcam resolved as in step 4 whose scene_commands execute("status") returns, and create_scene_source_connection, create_sketch_render_connection and generate_render_sketch on this MOVIOLA connection. If the director chose the Mac worker, or a Job for these Scenes is already queued for it (the director says so, or an earlier call returned its sceneSketch.jobId), take the worker route below. Otherwise, with those three, name the interactive route in one line and run steps 2–6 here without ordinary generate_storyboard for these Scenes, which would queue the same Cuts for a worker.
- The Mac worker route is for a director who chose it and for a Job already queued from the web Editor or an earlier call; follow that Job and do not also work its Cuts here. For a new Job the director's word is the only readiness check — no tool reports a worker before a Job exists — so unless they already said so, have them confirm their worker is running signed in to this same MOVIOLA account and environment; it claims only that account's Jobs. Then call ordinary generate_storyboard with draft_id, the 3D sceneIds and skill_version (plus pipelineMode while unsaved); while the saved inputs are unchanged, the same call for the same Scenes joins a queued Job rather than queueing another. Follow sceneSketch.jobId as step 6 describes.
- With neither the interactive capabilities nor a confirmed worker, do not queue a Job only because this session cannot execute one: nothing would claim it and its Cuts would sit at waiting_for_mac. Name what is missing and let the director choose — connect Blender with the MOVIOLA extension here, start the Mac worker, or switch the Scene to 2D — and report Sketch generation as pending. Both routes serve only a Scene whose current source is a .blend revision.
- **A Scene with no published source, or whose current source is server-built (v2), gets its 3D Sketch from the VCam Stills the director chooses.** Ordinary generate_storyboard draws a v2 Scene on the server, without a Mac worker, when every requested Cut has a current Still framing (step 5): the server draws each Cut's framing and generates its Sketch from that render after the call returns. serverSketches.jobId is one Job for those Cuts: get_job_status on it lists each Cut with its status, its render Sketch sketchJobId to follow as in step 6, and the error of a Cut refused on its own; cancel_job on it stops the Cuts not started yet, while a Cut already being sent finishes and is charged (its note says so). As on the Mac route, a Cut that already has a Sketch gets the new one as a candidate, and calling again pays again; calling again while that Job runs joins it and draws again only its Cuts that failed (drawnAgain), which pays again. A ModuleNotFoundError for scene_commands, or Unknown Scene command for a command this page names, means an old extension: stop any take, install the moviola_vcam extension ZIP for this MOVIOLA release from https://vcam.vibeproduction.ai/install with Blender's Install from Disk over the old one, enable it and rerun execute("status").

*The test:* the target is resolved, one execution route is named — or what is missing for both — and every proposed execution step has an available tool or a named handoff.

## 2 · Read the Master as a Space

A single image constrains a useful blockout without determining every hidden surface.

- Inspect the actual Master/Plate images and the saved Scene/Cut direction. Identify the floor and room envelope, openings, dominant landmarks, object groups, depth layers, walking space and the camera view. Separate visible evidence from estimates of scale, occluded objects and the unseen reverse side.
- Review existing references first. Before paying for references of a Scene with no published source or a v2 source, tell the director that a 3D Sketch from them needs a VCam Still chosen for each Cut (step 1), and go on only if the director still wants the space. For a saved 3D Scene that needs new references, call generate_storyboard with draft_id, the named sceneIds, skill_version and prepareReferences=true under the valid paid authorization. Poll its returned job_id with get_job_status using the same draft_id; repeating the same inputs joins the running Job or returns its completed receipt. A failed Job can be explicitly retried. This prepares Look/Plate/Master without Cut generation, Cut quota reservation or automatic Meshy calls. Ordinary generate_storyboard is the Mac worker route from step 1, never reference preparation. Selected 2D Scenes in a mixed Draft still use the existing server path.
- After preparation, reread get_scene_3d_state and call get_scene_reference_image with draft_id, sceneId, snapshotId and kind=master or plate (look is optional; a completed snapshot without one returns reference_kind_absent, so read master or plate instead). Inspect the actual returned pixels. Retain identity: Project/Draft/Scene, sourceId, snapshotId, kind, byteLength and sha256. The access URL is only a download location and may expire; it is not the reference identity. The read verifies the bytes against the receipt and reports stale or superseded references. If inputs changed, review the reasons before explicitly preparing a new snapshot; a locally written approved flag does not establish approval. renderer.status=outdated on a referencesReady snapshot means an older Plate/Master renderer baked it: it still builds and Sketches, and ordinary preparation keeps returning it without a provider call. Tell the director; only when they ask, call generate_storyboard again with prepareReferences=true and refreshReferences=true — a paid Plate/Master re-bake that becomes the current snapshot.
- Keep the reconstruction choices in the scene recipe: the references used, assumptions about dimensions and unseen layout, Scene instructions and each Cut's visual intent. Resolve uncertainties that would change a requested shot with the director; use stated reversible estimates for ordinary Low blocking.

*The test:* each important spatial choice traces to a visible reference, saved direction or recorded assumption.

- **A local Meshy job from before the server path is recovered, never repeated.** Skill 0.1.20 and earlier made new models in Blender with prepare_asset and submit_asset, each leaving a job directory with its job.json; MOVIOLA VCam 0.5.0 refuses both commands and only reads such a job. With a taskId: execute("poll_asset", directory=that job directory) and execute("download_asset", directory=the same), then execute("inspect_asset", directory=the same, inspection_directory=a new directory), execute("review_asset", directory=the same, inspection_directory=that directory, notes={mesh,texture}) after viewing its five views, execute("register_asset", directory=the same, library=the local library, metadata={assetId,revisionId,label,category,tags,dimensionsMeters,pivot,frontAxis}), and, to share it, execute("publish_shared_asset", asset=that one registered revision directory, api_origin=the API origin of step 4) with MOVIOLA_PAT in Blender's environment; a rerun returns the same receipt. state submission-unknown may already be billed: only the director's explicit match, execute("reconcile_asset", directory=that job directory, task_id=the matched Meshy task, evidence=how input and submission time were matched), resolves it. Until then do not match, isolate or prepare a server generation for that object, which could pay for it twice; report it pending. A job never sent stays unsent. Never delete a job, GLB or Scene file, and never publish a whole library. A Mac worker leaves local jobs to the director.

*The test:* every modeled instance pins a published shared revision (or a library revision already pinned), reused or generated once on the server with its match, generation and review receipts and an asset record written before each paid call — or is reported unresolved with its reason. Nothing was modeled locally or by another provider.

## 4 · Assemble and Review the Space

Build one coherent room that supports the intended Cut viewpoints.

- A Scene source connection to Blender serves only to frame and capture the Cuts (steps 5 and 6) of a Scene whose current source is still a .blend revision; a .blend edited by hand can no longer be published (below). For such a Scene, call create_scene_source_connection with draft_id and sceneId after setting the Scene mode. Through the existing Blender MCP Python executor, inspect bpy.context.preferences.addons and resolve the enabled module whose final name is moviola_vcam (normally bl_ext.user_default.moviola_vcam). An extension folder on disk does not prove it is enabled; only that list does. If none or several match, resolve the intended enabled extension first. Obtain execute with importlib.import_module(module + ".scene_commands").execute. Use that installed namespace to share the UI/session mutation gate; adding another checkout to sys.path can create a separate gate. Call execute("connect", api_origin=the API origin below, handoff=the returned handoff). It checks the issued connectionId and exact Project/Draft/Scene before storing the scoped grant in local Keychain. Keep the long-lived MOVIOLA token out of Blender files and recipes.
- **api_origin is the server, not the MCP endpoint.** A Mac worker session uses the API origin its prompt names and never runs `claude mcp list` or `codex mcp get`, which read the director's own servers, not the job's. Elsewhere, read this connection's MCP URL from the client's own config, the url alone and never its headers or token: `claude mcp list`, or `codex mcp get moviola --json | jq -r .transport.url`, which honours `$CODEX_HOME`. Keep its scheme://host[:port] and drop the trailing /mcp or /mcp/, so `https://<host>/mcp` gives `https://<host>`. A URL with any other path, a query or credentials does not reduce to an origin; ask. With a work folder the project card's server line must reduce to that same origin; if it does not, the card belongs to another server, so say so and do not connect. Pass the one origin to connect and connect_sketch alike.
- Poll execute("status") until operation.state is completed or failed. Run execute("verify") to recheck live authority, then inspect connection, blenderScene, blendFile and binding. execute("bind") verifies the connection and binds only the selected Blender Scene; it refuses a different existing binding. Save the working .blend explicitly to retain that binding. A busy Scene cannot accept another mutation.
- **The server assembles the Scene; Blender is not needed for it.** Call build_scene_source(draft_id, scene_id, snapshot_id=the current completed snapshotId from get_scene_3d_state, cut_ids=the explicit requested Cut IDs, recipe=the layout recipe below). It freezes that snapshot's Master/Plate identities, the saved Scene and Cut instructions and the Project Characters, and returns buildId with status queued at once; the same Scene, recipe and inputs return the same build. A recipe the server cannot read is refused at once with each bad field's path (invalid_recipe), an actor whose characterId is not a Project Character with character_mismatch, a part, or a sharedRevisionId drawn whole, that is not published with revision_unavailable (the model named beside parts only needs its passing review, so a model whose own label attempt failed is still drawn as its published parts), and a part that was not split from its object's sharedRevisionId with part_mismatch; fix the recipe and call again. Building is free.
- The layout recipe is JSON in the glTF frame: +Y up, metres, each object's front on its local +Z. It is {schemaVersion:1, axes:"right-handed-y-up-front-plus-z-camera-minus-z-y-up", name, observations, assumptions:{dimensions,occlusion,reverseLayout}, objects, camera, review:{center,distance}}. Each object has a unique objectId, kind (environment, prop or actor) and worldMatrix, a row-major 4×4 that places the object's bottom centre, and exactly one of: sharedRevisionId for a revision pinned in step 3, which the server scales to its catalog dimensions and turns to face +Z, with parts:[part revisionIds] beside it on a prop or environment to draw that model as those published parts (step 3); box:{size:[x, y up, z depth], color} for a primitive; or, for an actor only, mannequin:{body,pose} in place of sharedRevisionId or box: body male, female or child and pose stand, walk, sit or point. An actor also names its Project characterId, and only an actor does. Take each pose from the saved Scene and Cut instructions and follow the Master only when they name none; a Master that shows a seated person standing does not decide the pose. When the instructions seat a person, also place what they sit on, such as a chair. One build holds one pose per actor: when the requested Cuts give the same person different poses, ask the director which pose this build holds before building. The mannequin faces +Z, so its worldMatrix rotation is the direction that person faces in the Master; turned the wrong way, the Sketch draws them from behind. Camera uses the existing Cut Setup camera schema; it becomes the Scene camera that the master-view image shows. Record observed structure in observations, separately from each estimate in assumptions. The server adds the rest: one Cut camera per cut_ids entry, cut-camera-<cutId> as a copy of that camera with the Cut's order in its Scene, and a blockout light placed from review.center and review.distance. Treat that light as estimated blockout lighting, not lighting recovered from the Master. The objectId blockout-light and the cut-camera- prefix are the server's.
- Poll get_scene_source_build(draft_id, build_id) every few seconds while status is queued or building; it only reads. built returns the JSON with the five review PNGs after it in views order: master-view through the recipe camera, then front, side, reverse and top around review.center. failed returns error.code, error.message and gates (budget, structure, images, validator, loader, render), naming the model a failure came from; when error.retryable is true, call the same build_scene_source again, and otherwise fix the recipe. A recipe holds at most 1000 objects, each part instance counting as one, and its placed models at most 10 million triangles in all; scene_too_heavy and render_timeout mean the Scene is too heavy to draw, so use fewer objects or lighter models. For a correction call build_scene_source with the corrected recipe, keeping stable objectIds and pinned shared revisions. A new asset revision is a separate choice.
- View all five images. Compare silhouette, major proportions, openings, landmarks, depth, occlusion, which way each mannequin faces and usable Cut camera positions with the actual Master/Plate and Cut instructions. Also check each mannequin’s pose against the saved Scene and Cut instructions, and that a seated one has what it sits on. Correct the recipe and build again before publishing. Then call publish_scene_source_build(draft_id, build_id, images_digest=the imagesDigest returned with those five images, review={landmarks,depth,occlusion,poses,cutCameraSpace}, reason=one line for the Decision Memo), with specific nonempty observations for each key; poses names each actor’s pose and whether the Scene, a Cut or the Master set it. Another build's digest is refused with review_mismatch.
- Publishing makes the build the Scene's current source revision and is free. When the Scene already has a current source, its Cut Setups become history, so confirm with the director first. The result names revisionId and currentRevisionId; get_scene_source_upload with requestId=the buildId, or list_scene_source_revisions, confirms it, and publishing the same build again returns the same revision. reference_stale (the Scene, its Cuts, Characters or references changed after the build) and current_revision_conflict (another revision was published since) both need a new build_scene_source call. A server-built source is a glTF package (schemaVersion 2 in list_scene_source_revisions), not a .blend. The installed VCam extension restores only .blend ZIP sources, so never restore or frame it in Blender. Nothing can frame its Cuts yet (step 5), so a published v2 source does not lead to a Sketch for now.
- **A .blend source is read-only on the server.** A hand-edited Blender Scene cannot be published: execute("publish", directory=a new local directory) is refused with scene_package_v1_read_only, and a local save or uploaded bytes never prove publication. Published .blend revisions (schemaVersion 1 in list_scene_source_revisions) stay listed and restorable, and while one is still the Scene's current source its Cut Setups, renders and Sketch generation go on as steps 5 and 6 say. The only way to change the space is to build and publish a server source from a corrected recipe as above, and that ends this Scene's 3D Sketches for now: once a glTF revision is current, the Scene cannot return to a .blend revision, the Cut Setups made on the .blend revision stay history, and nothing can frame a Cut on the glTF source yet (step 5). Say exactly that and get the director's confirmation before publishing; without it, keep the .blend source and report the change as pending. A Mac worker session never builds or publishes a source.
- Use list_scene_source_revisions to inspect published revisions and currentRevisionId; includePending=true additionally reports incomplete publications and pointer conflicts. To change the server selection, only when the director asks, call select_scene_source_revision with an explicit glTF revisionId (schemaVersion 2) and the currentRevisionId just read as expectedCurrentRevisionId; a .blend revision is refused with scene_package_v1_read_only. A conflict requires rereading and reconciling the choice, not automatically resubmitting.
- For a working copy of a published .blend revision, call execute("restore", revision_id=the chosen published revision, directory=a new local directory), poll status, and inspect workingCopy. It validates package bytes and dependencies in an isolated Blender process. execute("open") opens that verified copy in a separate Blender process, preserving current work. Downloading a version does not select it on the server.
- After a lost .blend publish response or a restart, do not execute("retry", receipt=the saved publish.json path): the server refuses a .blend request that is begun again or still pending with scene_package_v1_read_only. Read get_scene_source_upload with its requestId instead: complete means it was published before, and pending can no longer be finished. Keep the files, report it, and never send the saved request to another Scene.

*The test:* the reviewed space is recoverable from the published package and has a returned source revision.

## 5 · Frame from Saved Editor Intent

The render is the camera and composition reference for the AI Sketch.

- Plan all requested Cut cameras together: each Cut has its own camera in the one Scene source. A server build (step 4) holds a camera object for each of its cut_ids but no Cut setup; a Cut gets one only from a VCam Still the director chooses (the paragraph on a v2 source below). In a .blend source each Cut camera is "Cut <number> camera" with stable object ID cut-camera-<cutId> in the Cameras Collection. get_framing returns that Cut's camera. Use its objectId in frame_cut; save_setup, apply_setup and capture_sketch use it as well. A Cut is never framed on another Cut's camera, and applying one Cut's setup leaves every other camera where it stands. A .blend source whose current revision lacks a requested Cut's camera, such as a Cut added later, cannot gain one: a camera added to the working copy reaches the server only through a .blend publication, which is refused (step 4), and a Cut left without its own camera is refused while another Cut's camera is active. Do not add_cut_camera, and do not create Cut cameras with Blender MCP code. Tell the director that this Cut cannot get a 3D Sketch now. A server source built with that Cut in cut_ids would hold its camera, but publishing it moves the whole Scene to a glTF source for good, where every Cut of the Scene then needs a VCam Still chosen for it (step 4): offer it only with that said. Only switching the whole Scene to 2D generates that Cut's Sketch. In a Scene where a Cut's current setup is manual (below), do not replace the source: that Scene keeps its published source.
- Without cut-cameras-v1, frame every Cut on the active camera, keep each framing in that Cut's own saved setup and apply_setup it before a later capture of that Cut; name the missing capability so the director can update the MOVIOLA extension. Reuse those cameras and the same Scene/assets for sequential capture/register/generate work; do not rebuild the Scene or wait for human review between Cuts. Local camera creation/rendering makes no provider call.
- **A v2 (server-built) source frames a Cut only from a VCam Still the director chooses.** Blender and frame_cut cannot publish a Cut setup on it. list_scene_vcam reads the Takes and Stills filmed on the Scene's VCam Set. Call use_vcam_still only when the director has said which Still to use for which Cut; never choose a Still yourself, and never match one to a Cut by its start camera name. A Still with framing.usable false cannot frame a Cut: still_other_version means it was filmed on another version of the Scene's Set, set_filming_reference that the Scene uses an uploaded Set, and still_source_changed that the Scene's 3D changed after VCam was connected, so the director connects VCam again and saves a new Still. use_vcam_still saves the Still's camera as the Cut's manual setup (below), selects it, draws it with the server renderer and returns the render with its PNG; it is free, and the same Still returns the same setup and render. Look at the PNG, then continue with step 6 using that renderId exactly as for a registered Blender render. When its render is null, renderError says why and the setup stays chosen: call render_cut_setup(draft_id, scene_id, cut_id, setup_revision_id=that setup ID), which draws any current setup of a v2 source the same way. Without a chosen Still, report those Cuts as pending for this reason and offer 2D (step 1). Do not connect Blender, capture_sketch or register_sketch for it. render_unavailable means the server renderer was busy: call again. source_not_renderable means the setup is on a v1 .blend source: use the Blender route below. raster_too_large names the server renderer's limit, 8192 pixels a side and 7680 x 4320 in all: that setup's raster is too large to draw.
- Use get_cut_framing_input with draft_id, sceneId and cutId to read the saved shotSize, cameraAngle, composition, focusSubject, lensType, cameraMovement and visible action with inputDigest and published object IDs. Read list_cut_setups for the selected setup, actual camera manifest and framing choices. Open the verified working copy of the exact source revision. An old setup may be applied through execute("apply_setup", revision_id=the setup ID, cut_id=cutId), which restores the baseline before absolute overrides; test A→B→A. Application alone does not certify that setup against new Editor input. To change the saved selection, use select_cut_setup with selection={schemaVersion:1, setupRevisionId, expectedSetupRevisionId:the just-read current ID or null}; a setup made on a revision that is not the current source cannot be selected, and selecting the setup already selected changes nothing. A locked Cut refuses every setup publication and selection, with or without framing, with cut_locked: tell the director, and unlock it with set_cut_lock only on their word.
- Call execute("prepare_framing", cut_id=cutId, directory=a new input directory), poll status, then execute("get_framing", inputs=the returned framingInputs path). Inspect the actual Scene objects, worldBounds and camera. Resolve focusSubject to published focusObjectIds. Derive numeric camera worldMatrix, projection, lensMm or orthoScale, shift and raster from those dimensions and the saved Cut intent. For each of shotSize, cameraAngle, composition, subjects, lens and staticMoment, explain which actual target/camera choices satisfy it; record assumptions separately. A preset name or forwarded cutInstructions is not a framed Cut. If targets are ambiguous, instructions conflict or the source lacks the required view, name what must be clarified or corrected in Editor/the Scene before continuing.
- Interpret cameraMovement as one named staticMoment of the still. clipCameraMovement belongs to Animatic; keep it out of this framing decision. Call execute("frame_cut", inputs=the prepared path, camera=the numeric camera, framing={inputDigest, focusObjectIds, choices:{shotSize,cameraAngle,composition,subjects,lens,staticMoment}, assumptions}). Inspect the applied camera and blocking. Then call execute("save_setup", cut_id=cutId, directory=a new receipt directory, expected_setup_revision_id=the currentSetupRevisionId just read, including null). Poll until the server receipt is complete. On a conflict reread and resolve the new intent; keep the saved request unchanged.
- Call execute("capture_sketch", directory=a new capture directory) after resolving unsaved source/camera changes. execute("get_sketch", directory=the capture) exposes the PNG and frozen registration intent. Use create_sketch_render_connection, then execute("connect_sketch", api_origin=the same API origin, handoff=the full result). execute("register_sketch", directory=the capture) and poll status. Retain Project/Draft/Scene/Cut, inputDigest, source/setup revisions, renderId, requestId and PNG digest. The render grant remains scoped to local render work; it cannot authorize paid generation.
- Read list_sketch_renders to confirm the exact uploaded renderId and current setup. Visual review is optional for the first pass: do not require six written assessments or pause for per-Cut approval before generating. If the director requests a review, inspect get_sketch_render_image and get_sketch_render_reviews, then record honest observations with stage_sketch_review/review_sketch; do not fabricate passing assessments to start generation.
- A setup with manual is the director's hand-set camera: its manifest camera applies as saved, and manual.input is the Editor direction saved when it was set. It has no framing choices, is not an AI framing, and its numbers never become shot size, lens type or other Editor fields. While it is the current setup without reasons, Generate reuses it: for that Cut do not prepare_framing, frame_cut, save_setup or select another setup, and do not publish a new source revision for its Scene. Reuse a complete render of that setup, or apply_setup it and capture/register a new render. If its reasons show an earlier Editor direction or source, Generate stops with manual_camera_stale; ask whether the director will set the camera again or reset it. save_setup with framing over it is refused with manual_camera_selected. Only when the director explicitly asks to reset framing to Editor, call reset_cut_framing with reset={schemaVersion:1, expectedSetupRevisionId:the just-read current ID}. It keeps every setup and render as history and makes no paid call; the next Generate frames that Cut from the saved Editor intent.
- Editor-only changes invalidate earlier framing even when source/setup IDs are unchanged. After a restart reread get_cut_framing_input. For a setup without manual, an editor_input_changed reason requires fresh prepare_framing → frame_cut → save_setup → capture_sketch → register_sketch. Keep prior renders as history. Recover lost registrations from the saved capture receipt in the original Scene.

*The test:* the current saved Editor digest, concrete camera setup and registered rendered pixels are linked; a visual-review receipt is optional.

## 6 · Complete the First Sketch Automatically

One authorized workflow continues through render-reference generation and first board placement.

- **Before each generate_render_sketch call, write its record.** It is one nonsecret JSON object, `{"apiOrigin":"…","projectId":"…","draftId":"…","sceneId":"…","cutId":"…","renderId":"…","request":{…},"jobId":null,"result":null}`: apiOrigin is the API origin Blender connected to (the capture manifest.json apiOrigin), or for a render_cut_setup render the api_origin step 4 resolves, and request is the exact request object you send; skill_version travels beside it as the current version and is not part of the request's identity. With a work folder the record is one line `Sketch 생성 요청: <record>` under `아직 안 한 것` in that Scene's section of the target Draft's own plan. Each change to it — the line before the call, jobId on the response, result once the Job settles — is a fresh reread, an edit of that line alone and put_work_file of the whole file in the same step, so the server's copy holds the request whichever side a later sync keeps. Without a folder it is generation-<requestId>.json beside registration.json in that render's capture directory, or in a new local directory for a render_cut_setup render. jobId is the response's job_id. result stays null until the Job completes or fails, then becomes {status, selection:selection.status, candidateId:candidate.cutImageId} or its error. When the call answers generation_in_progress instead, this request was never accepted: write "hold":"generation_in_progress" into the record the same way, and follow the Job it names as below without writing that Job's jobId here. Identities are IDs — renderId, jobId and candidateId; the record holds no token, handoff code, grant or image URL.
- Within the existing paid authorization for the named Cuts, continue immediately after each render registration: write the record, then call generate_render_sketch with draft_id, sceneId, cutId, renderId, skill_version and request={schemaVersion:1, requestId:a fresh UUID, selectIfEmpty:true}. Omit reviewId on the normal first pass; never require per-Cut review, generation confirmation or adoption. The Project Sketch model/style uses the render as the primary composition reference and Master/Character as appearance references. Upload-only grants cannot authorize paid generation; use the authenticated MOVIOLA MCP seat under the user-authorized workflow.
- Keep each job_id. The server finishes accepted provider jobs in the background, including after restart; get_job_status reports progress and selection.status. selected means the first Sketch was placed on the board; preserved means an existing selection, changed inputs or access prevented automatic placement. nextAction reads the Job first: reconcile_generation while it waits with submission_unknown (below), poll_job while it runs, review_error once it failed, read_board once its Sketch is on the board. Only a completed result left off the board reads its selectionReasons: review_candidate with none, unlock_cut for a locked Cut (set_cut_lock, only on the director's word), stop_using_set when the Scene took an uploaded Set for filming after the request (the director detaches that Set on the web, then the candidate can be adopted), and otherwise reframe_render_review_generate. A generate_render_sketch call or an adoption refused for the same causes names the same nextAction.
- **After a restart or a lost response, resolve every record whose result is null before any new paid call.** Its apiOrigin, Draft, Scene and Cut must be the ones this connection reaches. Then, in order: (1) with a jobId, read get_job_status. (2) Without one, read list_sketch_renders for the Cut; an activeGeneration carrying the record's requestId and renderId is that request still running — record its jobId and follow it. (3) Otherwise read list_sketch_candidates, and for each candidate whose inputRenderId is the record's renderId call get_job_status with its imageMetadata.jobId: the one whose requestId is the record's is the result whose response was lost, and a refused one may be this request seen from another account. The render's other candidates are separate deliberate attempts: each is claimed only through its own record, and one no record claims is reported as unclaimed — never a reason to generate or adopt. (4) Only when none of these names it, the record carries no hold, and the director has confirmed this connection signs in as the account that recorded it, resend the identical recorded request — same renderId, same request. Request IDs belong to one account: the same request from another account is a new paid Job. If the server already holds the request, the replay returns its Job and charges nothing again; if it never arrived, this is its first charge, under the original authorization. A generation_in_progress answer holds the record as above.
- A record stays **unresolved** — reported with its reason, its result left null — when its target is not one this connection reaches, when get_job_status refuses its Job or a Job of its render's candidates (it answers only the requesting account, in the Job's original Draft), and while its Job waits with waitingReason submission_unknown (nextAction reconcile_generation), which is never resubmitted under any request ID. An hour after that Job started the server settles it by itself: with a saved provider acceptance id it collects the result, and the Job goes on to complete or fail; with none it closes the Job as failed with error submission_unconfirmed. Until then a new first pass on that Cut answers generation_in_progress. Write either end into the record as its result; after submission_unconfirmed the provider may still have run the request, so another attempt is the director's decision. A held record is different from a lost response: it is known never to have been accepted, so report it as held and never resend it on its own — not even after the Job that held the Cut finishes; it folds away once the director decides. With no record at all, follow any activeGeneration, report the board's Sketch (list_sketch_renders currentSketchInputRenderId names its render) and the candidates list_sketch_candidates shows, and report that Cut as unresolved; recovery reads and starts nothing. A recovered result keeps the selection it got: a preserved candidate waits for an explicit adoption. Another paid attempt comes only from the director's new instruction, as a new requestId with its own record, reported as a new generation.
- On the Mac worker route, poll sceneSketch.jobId with get_job_status and read status first, never a Cut count. completed — granted only after the server verifies a completed AI Sketch receipt for every requested Cut — and failed, with its error, are final whatever stage still says, as is cancelled, a Job ended with cancel_job or the web's Cancel. While the Job is active, report its stage: waiting_for_mac (queued, or the worker stopped renewing its claim), then preparing_scene, rendering and generating_sketches. paused carries the worker's error: report it, and once the director has checked it, the same ordinary generate_storyboard call (or Generate in the web Editor) resumes that Job rather than starting a new paid run; cancel_job ends it instead. A Job that failed because 3D Sketch cannot be generated for its Scene now was queued before step 1's refusal existed: do not queue it again. Then read each Cut's result as below.
- A Cut's Job may also have started on the web or in VCam. generate_render_sketch then returns generation_in_progress with activeGeneration {jobId, requestId, renderId, status}: follow that Job with get_job_status (same account) or list_sketch_candidates, and do not start another paid request for the Cut. VCam generates and adopts only through the Sketch connection the director issues on the web; never create or request that code for them. Its Jobs and adoption receipts belong to the issuing account, so recover them with the same request IDs as your own.
- After the first pass, read the board and list_sketch_candidates, and inspect actual output with get_sketch_candidate_image. Report completed Cuts and visible limitations together; the director reviews the finished first Sketches, not intermediate checklists. Camera provenance does not guarantee pixel-perfect composition. Fix a wrong view at its camera in Blender and regenerate only the requested Cuts. Additional paid attempts require authorization beyond the existing run.
- Regeneration preserves an existing Sketch. To replace it after comparison, call adopt_sketch_candidate with the exact candidateId and request={schemaVersion:1, requestId:a fresh UUID, expectedPriorSketch:the just-read currentSketch.imageUrl or null}. This free selection step is for replacements or recovered candidates, not a prerequisite for initial production. Keep conflict receipts and reread competing choices rather than overwriting them. A conflict is final for its requestId: clear what its reasons and nextAction name, then adopt with a new requestId. Adopting the Sketch already on the board changes nothing.
- For adoption response loss use get_sketch_candidate_adoption with the same candidateId/requestId, or resend the identical adoption request. Then reread list_sketch_candidates and inspect currentSketch.candidateId through get_sketch_candidate_image. That reads the selected AI Sketch even when a Final exists; get_cut_image/get_scene_board may prefer Final. An old adopted receipt proves that request completed, not that it remains selected. Keep receipts and images on revoked permission, moved/deleted Cuts or changed source/setup; resolve the reported scope without retargeting old requests.
- Legacy raw-render selections and adoption receipts remain readable with get_sketch_adoption; adopt_sketch_render only replays an existing receipt. New raw selection still returns render_reference_generation_required: Blender pixels are the input, never the AI Sketch output. The normal flow is saved Editor direction → Cut camera → registered render → generate_render_sketch → first board placement. The local worker executes this workflow for queued 3D Cuts; use the bound render path instead of aiDerivation.

*The test:* every requested Cut has an AI Sketch on its initially empty board slot with render/input/source/setup lineage, or a named pending, failed, preserved or unresolved result. Existing Sketches require an explicit replacement choice.

## 7 · Stop at the Requested Stage

A Sketch deliverable is complete without a phone.

- For a Sketch-only request, report the stored Scene revision, adopted Cut Sketches, assumptions and unresolved work. Finalize is optional and needs separate visual comparison when requested; matching provenance does not prove the AI preserved composition. VCam recording and Take upload belong to the later Animatic task. Speech to World and higher asset tiers remain separate work.

Complete when: Each 3D Sketch request followed exactly one route — interactive here, a Mac worker Job read by status and stage, or a v2 Scene's serverSketches Job — or was reported pending with the missing capability named; no Job was queued for a worker nobody confirmed. A Cut of a v2 source was framed only from a VCam Still the director named, or reported pending for one with 2D offered. On a finished route the Scene source is published with a returned revision, and the authorized first pass produces AI Sketches on empty board slots without intermediate review/adoption stops. Every modeled object was reused from a published revision, or generated once on the server, reviewed from its renders and published, then fetched by exact revision — or reported unresolved with its reason; nothing fell back to local Meshy. Every paid asset call had its asset record written before it went out, and a restart resumed each record without a new isolation or charge. Every generate_render_sketch request had its record written before it went out, and every lost response was resolved from that record to its own Job or candidate, or reported unresolved, without a new paid request. Report pending, failed, preserved or unresolved results accurately. No Finalize or VCam step is required.
